title: rig.yaml — rig-cli declarative config
description: The committed source of truth for a repo's setup (and ~/.config/rig/config.yaml). See docs/config-schema.md for the human-readable reference.

agent_tools_source.description: the agent-tools checkout to apply FROM (default: auto-detect)

stack.description: the repo's stack preset `l1/lang[/framework]` (e.g. mobile/swift/swiftui, frontend/ts/react, backend/python). l1 in mobile|frontend|backend|desktop|embedded|system; lang required; framework optional. Selects by-stack skills. Global default is optional; a per-repo value is expected (soft-required).

defaults.description: cross-category fallback targets + the on-conflict policy.

on_conflict.description: what apply does when a target already exists

scripts.description: repo-level commands consumed by the standalone `dev run <name>` CLI (alex-mextner/dev-cli).

dev.description: repo-level development server and e2e metadata consumed by the standalone `dev` CLI (alex-mextner/dev-cli, provisioned like any other ecosystem tool via the `tools:` block).

server.description: development server metadata for `dev` lifecycle commands.

script.description: name of the top-level scripts entry that starts the dev server

url.description: base URL the development server serves

ready_url.description: URL the dev CLI can poll before running e2e

port.description: a single known TCP port the dev CLI may check (fallback alias for `ports: [port]` — dev-cli reads `ports` first, then falls back to this)

ports.description: known TCP ports the dev CLI may check

process_matchers.description: process command substrings the dev CLI may use to identify owned server processes

logs_root.description: directory where the dev CLI writes server logs

e2e.description: end-to-end test metadata for `dev` lifecycle commands.

script.description: name of the top-level scripts entry that runs e2e tests

requires_server.description: whether e2e expects the dev server to be running

logs_root.description: directory where the dev CLI writes e2e logs

jobs.description: named e2e jobs keyed by job name

additionalProperties.description: one named e2e job consumed by the standalone `dev` CLI (alex-mextner/dev-cli).

script.description: name of the top-level scripts entry that runs this e2e job

requires_server.description: whether this e2e job expects the dev server

artifacts_root.description: directory where this e2e job writes artifacts

logs_root.description: directory where this e2e job writes logs

skills.description: advisory markdown rules copied into the agent skills dir (opt-out model).

known.description: hand-installed skill dir names on disk that rig does NOT manage but should report as known (informational), not as drift — see docs/config-schema.md#provenance

harness_link.description: also symlink each installed skill into the harness discovery dir

universal.description: the universal skill set (opt-out via disable / opt-in via enable).

by_type.description: by-type skill bundles for the detected project type.

enable.description: which by-type bundles to install whole

by_stack.description: by-stack skills auto-selected by the repo's declared `stack` (hierarchical prefix match); tune with disable / per-item overrides.

disable.description: by-stack skill item names (`by-stack/<l1>/<lang>[/<fw>]/<name>`) to drop even though the declared stack would select them

items.description: per-skill overrides keyed by `by-stack/<l1>/<lang>[/<fw>]/<name>` (`enabled: true` force-adds an off-stack skill; `enabled: false` drops one)

agent_hooks.description: programmatic guards that block before a side effect (no-verify, secrets, raw merge).

target_kind.description: legacy ignored scaffold key; accepted for old configs but not used for rendering

known.description: hook ids (or full descriptor stems) another installer wrote on disk that rig does NOT manage but should report as known (informational), not as drift — see docs/config-schema.md#provenance

worktree_only.description: enforce the worktree-only workflow: gates TWO hooks. worktree-only-writes DENIES an Edit/Write while the checkout sits on the default branch (main/master); pin-primary-worktree DENIES a git checkout/switch that would move the repo's PRIMARY worktree onto anything but the default branch. Opt-IN, default OFF — a repo that works directly on main (e.g. 3d-cli) leaves it off and is never blocked. No self-service env bypass — each hook has its OWN hatch var: a deliberate one-off Edit/Write on main is requested via RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_WORKTREE_ONLY_WRITES="<justification>"; a one-off git checkout/switch in the primary checkout via RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_PIN_PRIMARY_WORKTREE="<justification>" (both: tg approval, deny-by-default; bare 1 rejected). (Alex tg#5742, tg#6462/tg#6477.)

orchestrator_only.description: keep the orchestrator thin: the orchestrator-stays-thin hook warns on the first inline implementation Bash / code Edit by the main thread (delegate to a subagent), then blocks a repeat within its TTL. Read-only inspection (git status/ls/cat/grep/find, git worktree list) is never gated; tg/review/task are sanctioned orchestration, also never gated. Most gh is still delegated to a subagent — gh pr merge/create/close/edit, gh issue create/close/edit, gh release, any gh api mutation included. Two exceptions run inline: an unchained gh ship <PR#> alone on the line, and a fixed read-only allowlist (gh issue list/view, gh pr list/view/checks/diff, gh run list/view/watch, gh repo view, GET-only gh api with no -f/--field, -F/--raw-field, or --input). Opt-OUT, default ON — set false to exempt a repo that legitimately works inline (e.g. 3d-cli). No self-service env bypass; a one-off is requested via RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_ORCHESTRATOR_STAYS_THIN="<justification>" (tg approval, deny-by-default; bare 1 rejected). (Alex tg#5743, tg#7103; allowlist enforced by agent-tools#764, 2026-09-18.)

items.description: per-hook overrides (enabled / on_error) keyed by hook name

git_hooks.description: the global-hook dispatcher: your hooks run in every repo, even ones that hijack core.hooksPath.

set_global_hooks_path.description: wire it as git's global core.hooksPath

fragments.description: per-fragment overrides keyed by fragment name (secret-scan, …)

ci.description: vendor-neutral CI gates (secret-scan, codeql, dependency-review, ship, …).

known.description: workflow file stems this repo owns that collide with a catalog slot name on disk that rig does NOT manage but should report as known (informational), not as drift — see docs/config-schema.md#provenance

items.description: per-gate overrides (enabled / tier / variant / …) keyed by gate name

require_external_review.description: Machine-only GitHub-side external-review policy; other ship gates are unchanged.

external_review_owners.description: Exact owner logins covered by a false require_external_review; no wildcards.

mcp.description: MCP registrations (review, code-search) — callable from any agent.

known.description: MCP server names registered by something other than rig on disk that rig does NOT manage but should report as known (informational), not as drift — see docs/config-schema.md#provenance

items.description: per-server overrides (command / args / env / server / enabled) keyed by server name

command.description: server executable, or legacy command string when args is omitted

mode.description: machine-wide operating mode; `autonomous` provisions review/fix, quorum, escalation, and parallelism policy.

autonomous.description: policy knobs active when mode.name is autonomous.

max_iterations.description: maximum review/fix iterations before escalation or budget stop

decisions.description: decision-making policy before asking the user.

min_models.description: minimum distinct models in the quorum

escalation.description: when and how an agent may escalate to the user.

framework_skill.description: skill that defines escalation message behavior

require_parallel_worktree_comparison.description: compare independent worktree attempts before escalation

candidates.description: number of independent candidate implementations to compare

development_tools.description: extra allowlisted development-tool permission flows for autonomous mode.

allow.description: raw permission allow rules to add while in autonomous mode

reserve_slots.description: slots held back for urgent work

harness.description: the agent harness's auto/permission mode — provisioned, not hand-toggled.

kind.description: which harness to provision (skills-dir: claude-code/codex; native-discovery: opencode/omp; instruction-file: pi/commandcode; codex is also instruction-file via AGENTS.md). Every kind gets its own auto/permission-mode key written (claude-code permissions.defaultMode, codex approvals_reviewer, opencode permission.*, omp tools.approvalMode via the permissions approval action); pi/commandcode have no such setting and get a visible n/a note.

kinds.description: additional harnesses to provision alongside harness.kind. Use this when one machine runs multiple harnesses: the primary kind keeps its auto-mode/settings_path behavior, while additional kinds get skill discovery, agent-hook descriptors, any supported hook bridge, and their own auto-mode key (same auto intent). If agent_hooks.target pins descriptors to one explicit target, supported bridges are registered with a descriptor-dir override.

auto_mode.description: true → auto-accept tool calls; false → interactive — written per harness kind. A pinned mode: the primary kind knows overrides it (mode: auto means auto for every configured kind).

self_merge.description: true → add the ship allow rules (Bash(gh ship:*), Bash(*/pr-ship.sh:*), Bash(*/ship.sh:*)) to permissions.allow so the auto-mode Bash gate stops vetoing gh ship, PLUS the natural-language carve-out to autoMode.allow (clears the Merge-Without-Review + Self-Approval soft blocks for the agent's OWN PRs); auto-mode only; the Bash(gh pr merge:*) deny and every other classifier rule (incl. the anti-exfil hard rule) stay

mode.description: pin the exact permission value (overrides auto_mode map)

settings_path.description: override the per-harness settings/config/plugin path; absent means rig uses the harness-specific default

settings_paths.description: EXTRA claude-code user-scope settings.json files the auto-mode/permissions/hook-bridge writes also reach (each a .json path); only honored when the primary target is ~/.claude/settings.json

discover_config_dirs.description: auto-discover every ~/.claude-accounts/account-*/ (claude-rotate) config dir and treat its settings.json as a managed target alongside ~/.claude/settings.json — a `claude` started with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR reads ONLY that dir's settings, so without this no rig hook runs there

hook_bridge.description: wire the agents-hooks/v1 dispatcher into the supported harness config.

enabled.description: wire the supported harness hook-bridge dispatcher

python.description: the interpreter the dispatcher runs under

web_search.description: omp web_search provider exclude list, reconciled into ~/.omp/agent/config.yml.

enabled.description: provision providers.webSearchExclude when omp is a configured harness kind

exclude.description: provider ids web_search must never use, even as fallbacks; default [perplexity]

idle_ttl.description: omp task.agentIdleTtlMs grace window, reconciled into ~/.omp/agent/config.yml.

enabled.description: provision task.agentIdleTtlMs when omp is a configured harness kind

ms.description: idle-TTL grace window in ms before a yielded omp helper parks off hub list; default 300000 (5 min); <= 0 restores the old never-park behavior

enabled.description: provision skills.max_context_tokens when codex is a configured harness kind

max_context_tokens.description: Codex's context budget (tokens) for rendering the model-visible skills catalog; default 50000 raises Codex's own smaller stock default so a sizeable personal skill library is not silently truncated/omitted (openai/codex#24299). Only WRITTEN when the key is absent -- apply never clobbers a value already on disk

permissions.description: reconcile the harness permissions layer: the command allowlist + the deny/ask rule baselines.

kind.description: which harness's permissions to provision; null/absent means fan out to supported harness.kind plus harness.kinds

tools.description: command names to pre-allow (replaces the default set)

extra.description: command names to ADD on top of the set

disable.description: command names to drop from rig's desired set

allow_gh.description: pre-allow the GitHub CLI (gh); false opts out (sugar over disable: [gh]) — see the gh note in docs/config-schema.md for the residual risk this trades in

allow.description: raw permission-rule entries asserted present in the allow list, on TOP of the tool-derived ones

deny.description: permission-rule entries asserted present in the deny list (REPLACES the baked baseline)

ask.description: permission-rule entries asserted present in the ask list (REPLACES the baked baseline)

models.description: a daily cron that runs the model-freshness checker and proposes version bumps.

label.description: the launchd Label / crontab sentinel identity

agents_md.description: one canonical AGENTS.md + a CLAUDE.md symlink, so every harness reads the same instructions.

github.description: GitHub repository settings rig reconciles via gh api + agent-browser.

ruleset.description: a branch ruleset on the default branch (the modern branch-protection replacement).

required_conversation_resolution.description: require every review thread resolved before merge (required_review_thread_resolution)

dismiss_stale_reviews.description: dismiss stale approvals on a new push (dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push)

required_status_checks.description: contexts to require; empty emits no rule

admin_bypass.description: add the repo Admin role to bypass_actors

require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_.description: pull_request rule sub-param: GitHub's own extra-approval-for-unattributed-changes rule (documented for PRs opened under an app identity, e.g. Copilot). Mode-gated to false for autonomous-mode repos; otherwise unmanaged (not compared for drift, and preserved verbatim if an unrelated ruleset knob triggers a PUT).

merge.description: the repo merge-button policy (squash-only, auto-delete head branch, allow-auto-merge) via PATCH /repos.

squash_merge.description: allow_squash_merge (the only merge model by default)

delete_branch_on_merge.description: auto-delete the head branch on merge

allow_auto_merge.description: allow a PR to auto-merge when its gate is green

ghas.description: GitHub Advanced Security: dependency graph + vuln-alerts + Dependabot + secret-scanning + CodeQL.

actions.description: GitHub Actions permissions: enabled + allowed_actions + the default GITHUB_TOKEN scope.

browser.description: settings the REST API does NOT expose, driven via agent-browser (gated off at apply unless RIG_GH_BROWSER=1).

enabled.description: plan the agent-browser backend (status lists it)

tmux.description: rig-managed tmux configuration (persistence across reboots, plugin-init ordering).

conf_path.description: the user's tmux config rig migrates

cc_restore.description: per-window Claude Code resume by session id.

omp_restore.description: per-window omp (oh-my-pi) resume by session file.

codex_restore.description: per-window Codex CLI resume by session id.

boot.description: a launchd agent that brings tmux up after a reboot.

autosave.description: an INDEPENDENT launchd saver (decoupled from continuum's status-right hook); when on, continuum's own autosave is disabled so there is one authoritative saver.

enabled.description: provision the independent tmux-autosave launchd agent (StartInterval = continuum.save_interval minutes)

stale_after.description: minutes: rig doctor/status flags a mature live server whose newest save is older than this

pane_titles.description: pane-border-status titles (position + format), and separately dropping tmux's default clock+date from status-right.

format.description: pane-border-format value (no date/time token by default; must not contain '"', '\\', '$', '#(' (a shell-exec token), or a non-printable character other than a plain tab)

clear_status_right.description: when `enabled` is on, also clear tmux's default clock+date status-right; a SEPARATE toggle (nested under `enabled`) so status-right can be left alone while keeping the border title

focus_events.description: report terminal focus in/out events to programs running inside panes (tmux's `focus-events` option) — needed by editors/tools that react to focus.

clipboard.description: copy-mode clipboard integration: pipe a copy-mode selection (keyboard `prefix [`, `v`, `Enter`/`y`, or a mouse-drag release) through a resolved system-clipboard command, since tmux's own built-in copy-pipe-and-cancel bindings run with no pipe command by default (tmux paste buffer only, not the system clipboard). See `copy_mode.mode_keys` for the (independent) copy-mode key table.

enabled.description: provision the copy-mode clipboard key bindings

command.description: explicit clipboard-write command override ('' → auto-detect: macOS pbcopy; Linux wl-copy/xclip/xsel); must not contain '"', '\\', '$', '#(' (a shell-exec token), or a non-printable character other than a plain tab

copy_mode.description: the copy-mode key table (tmux's `mode-keys` option). tmux's own default is `emacs`, under which `Space` pages the view (not begin-selection) and a bare `v` is unbound, so a vim-style copy-mode workflow (`prefix [` then `v`/`Space` to select) silently does nothing. Rendered unconditionally, independent of `clipboard` settings.

env.description: rig-managed shell environment variables (GLOBAL, machine-wide): a generated file (`<generated_dir>/rig.env.sh`, one `export KEY=value` per `vars` entry) sourced by ONE spliced line in `rc_path`. Default `rc_path` is `~/.zshenv`, sourced by EVERY zsh invocation (login or not, interactive or not) so a var reaches non-interactive shells too.

enabled.description: provision the rig-managed shell env vars — see the block's own doc for the opt-in rule (block PRESENCE, not this key's default, decides)

rc_path.description: the shell startup file rig sources the generated env file from

gitignore.description: a rig-managed block in git's global core.excludesfile (ignores harness worktrees + the Spotlight sentinel machine-wide).

entries.description: the ignored paths inside the managed block

excludesfile.description: force a specific file instead of honoring core.excludesfile

spotlight.description: macOS Spotlight-exclude: drop .metadata_never_index into dependency/build dirs + a launchd re-sweep agent.

enabled.description: provision the Spotlight-exclude sweep + agent (opt-in, macOS)

deny.description: dependency/build dir basenames to exclude (REPLACES the default set)

extra.description: extra dir basenames to exclude (ADDS to the default set)

bun.description: GLOBAL bunfig: splice [install] linker=isolated and globalStore=true.

tools.description: the personal CLI tool ecosystem (tg/review/task/draw/…) rig installs + advertises at apply, by running each tool's own install.sh. rig also keeps a provisioned checkout FRESH: if a tool repo ships scripts/deploy.sh, apply runs it (ff-only git pull) even when already installed — opt-in per tool, non-fatal. Default OFF (opt-in): list tools under items. A per-MACHINE concern — belongs in the GLOBAL layer, not a committed rig.yaml.

target.description: managed PATH dir each tool symlinks its bin into

items.description: per-tool spec keyed by command name (repo / bin_dir / enabled)

additionalProperties.description: one declared tool: the repo whose install.sh rig runs, plus optional overrides.

repo.description: the tool's checkout dir (holds install.sh); default ~/xp/<name>-cli

bin_dir.description: override the managed PATH dir for this one tool

brew.description: Homebrew formulae this tool depends on at RUNTIME (not installed by the tool's own install.sh); rig installs any missing formula via `brew install` before running install.sh, and `rig status` flags a declared-but-absent formula as drift. Fails closed with an actionable error if `brew` itself is not on PATH. Default [] — no package dependency declared, the existing behavior for every tool that omits this key.

tg_ctl.description: the tg-ctl inbound daemon auto-started as a per-machine boot LaunchAgent (macOS).

codex_usage_hook.description: fold tg-ctl's Codex Stop usage-telemetry hook into rig's own codex hook bridge in ~/.codex/config.toml instead of tg-ctl writing its own ~/.codex/hooks.json (tg-cli#308)

tcc_watch.description: the TCC dialog-watcher daemon (Phase 1: detection-only), a per-machine boot LaunchAgent (macOS) that tails `log stream`'s com.apple.TCC subsystem and logs every permission-prompt-shaped event — defense-in-depth behind the eval-tool TCC deny-list (PR #488).

config_dir.description: watcher config + events.jsonl + launchd logs dir

python_bin.description: the python3 binary the daemon runs under

tgctl_reaper.description: the tgctl-reaper periodic sweep for orphaned tg-ctl/omp test-fixture helpers (agent-tools#697), a per-machine `StartInterval` LaunchAgent (macOS) that SIGKILLs provably-orphaned `omp acp` test fixtures every `interval_seconds`.

python_bin.description: the python3 binary the sweep runs under

internal_dev.description: internal development of the rig-ecosystem tools themselves (rig, tg-cli, review-cli, …): a per-repo COMMITTED opt-in that installs a post-commit git hook so a commit touching the daemon's source gracefully reloads the running daemon (tg-ctl restart) — zero manual restart.

auto_reload_on_commit.description: install a post-commit hook that reloads the daemon when a commit touches a daemon-source path (opt-in)

daemon_source_paths.description: repo-relative shell-glob patterns (POSIX `case`, `*` spans `/`) whose change in a commit triggers the reload

reload_command.description: the graceful reload command the hook runs on a match

ship_delegator.description: a per-repo .claude/scripts/pr-ship.sh delegator so `gh ship` works in this repo (ignored in .git/info/exclude).

linters.description: Rig-owned lint/format policy plus explicit reusable config carriers.

preview.description: show before/after lint finding counts when policy changes

rules.description: Rig-owned rule selection. Built-in defaults are inherited through global config and rig.yaml; inspect the effective result with `rig lint rules`.

all.description: enable every applicable known policy concept after provider selection/dedup; per-rule severity still wins

enable.description: individual rules to enable without enabling all

disable.description: individual rules to disable after defaults/groups/all

severity.description: final per-rule off|warn|error overrides; highest-precedence rule-policy setting

groups.description: rule-group toggles keyed by group name; `anti-slop: true` uses audited per-rule defaults rather than forcing every rule to error

additionalProperties.description: one deterministic directory bundle copied from agent-tools

items.description: extra config files keyed by label; each uses `{ tool, role, path, content|source, enabled }`.

additionalProperties.description: one explicit linter/formatter config file rig writes/reconciles.

content.description: literal desired content; mutually exclusive with source

source.description: agent-tools-relative canonical source file; mutually exclusive with content

project_tools.description: repo-local integration carriers for Haft, Serena, and Sverklo.

haft.description: Haft FPF/spec carriers plus optional Codex MCP registration.

project_name.description: Haft project name; defaults to the repo directory name

project_id.description: stable Haft project id; generated from project_name when omitted

codex_mcp.description: merge the Haft MCP server into .codex/config.toml

require_decision.description: require explicit decisions for high-impact work

allow_autonomy.description: allow autonomous Haft execution by default

project_name.description: Serena project name; defaults to the repo directory name

languages.description: Serena language ids; auto-detected when omitted

read_only.description: disable Serena editing tools for this project

sverklo.description: Sverklo global registry/index integration for this repo.

register.description: register this repo in the global Sverklo registry

reindex.description: run sverklo reindex during apply (off by default)

ecosystem_readme.description: writes/updates a marker-delimited '## Ecosystem' section in a target repo's README from one canonical, in-code tool registry (riglib.ecosystem_readme), so the hand-copied sibling-tool list every repo carries stops silently drifting (rig-cli#308). Default OFF (opt-in) — enable it, then `rig apply` inserts the section (or updates a stale one).

task.description: task-cli ticket-tracker routing for THIS repo (CTO decision #4136.4: hyperide -> Linear/HYP, every other repo -> GitHub Issues by default). task-cli reads this block directly (tasklib/config.py's rig_task_overlay) with LOWER precedence than a repo's own native task.yaml, so a repo that already keeps one is unaffected. Flat shorthands (team/project/repo/attachment_mode) and the nested github:/linear: sections may be used together in the same block; task-cli itself rejects a genuine collision between the two forms (e.g. both `team: X` and `linear: {team: Y}` set to different values) — this schema only checks the KEY SET, not that kind of cross-field conflict. `code_prefix` is a SEPARATE, unrelated concern folded into the same top-level `task:` block (rig-cli#217): a repo-unique task-code prefix consumed by ship.sh's review-quorum gate, reconciled by `rig apply` into `.ship-config` — see the leaf's own doc below. UB-23: `backend: tasks` selects the native Tasks-app backend (HTTPS REST), configured via the nested `tasks:` block (`url`/`team`/`attachment_mode`), mirroring `github:`/`linear:` below.

code_prefix.description: set when this repo's task-cli backend is GitHub Issues (bare #NNN, no ticket-code convention of its own). `rig apply` writes it into .ship-config's SHIP_TASK_CODE_PREFIX line, which ship.sh synthesizes into <PREFIX>-NNN from a bare #NNN in the branch name/PR body — never the bare number itself (review-cli's review-quorum store is a single global file keyed only by the code string, with no per-repo scoping, so two repos both deriving bare "#346" would collide). Must be 1-40 uppercase letters/digits — ship.sh ignores the whole .ship-config file otherwise. Unset = bare issue numbers are never picked up as task codes.

attachment_mode.description: how a screenshot/file gets attached to a Linear ticket: 'native' uploads it through Linear's own API as a real attachment (the default); 'link' never uploads a local file, only registers an already-hosted URL as-is (hyperide's default, HYP-1248 — raw uploads.linear.app image links 401 for a non-browser viewer)

projects.description: the cross-project registry (task-cli's own shape, not deeply modeled here)

github.description: GitHub Issues coordinates (used when backend: github-issues).

repo.description: owner/name, or 'auto' to detect from the git remote

linear.description: Linear coordinates + write behavior (used when backend: linear).

project.description: an optional Linear project id to scope create/list/search to

attachment_mode.description: same as the flat `attachment_mode` shorthand above, nested form

tasks.description: Tasks-app (native HTTPS REST) coordinates (used when backend: tasks).

url.description: the Tasks-app base URL, e.g. https://tasks-ultrabricks.vercel.app

team.description: the Tasks-app team/workspace key (e.g. UB, HYP)

attachment_mode.description: how a screenshot/file gets attached to a Tasks-app ticket: 'native' uploads it through the Tasks-app API, 'link' registers an already-hosted URL as-is
